Ford Taurus Buyer's Guide

The car that saved Ford, ruled the 1990s sales charts, and died a fleet queen — with a Yamaha-hearted SHO legend running through all of it. Every era, sorted.

By Bennett Hale · 4 chapters, about 8 min in all · Updated November 19, 2026 · Find one for sale

In this guide
  1. ●Overview
  2. 11986–1995
  3. 2The SHO story
  4. 31996–2007
  5. 42008–2019

No American car of the past 40 years carried a bigger arc than the Taurus. The 1986 jelly bean rewrote sedan design and won Motor Trend's Car of the Year; the 1992 car took the best-seller crown from Honda and held it 5 straight years; the oval 1996 redesign handed that crown to the Camry; the 2000s turned it into a rental fleet queen; and the 2010 revival made it a 365-hp flagship and a police car before the last one left Chicago on March 1, 2019. Roughly 8 million sold in 33 years.

For today's buyer the Taurus is 3 different propositions: dirt-cheap honest transportation (1992–2007), a surprisingly good used flagship (2010–2019), and a genuine enthusiast collectible — the SHO, whose Yamaha-built engines get their own chapter.

Quick picks

  • Best used buy: a 2013–2019 with the 288-hp 3.5 or the 25-mpg 2.0 EcoBoost — enormous, safe, comfortable, and cheaper than the equivalent Japanese sedan every time.
  • The legend: a 1989–1991 SHO with the 5-speed. 220 Yamaha horsepower, 6.6 to 60 in Car and Driver's test, and values climbing from nothing.
  • The modern muscle one: a 2013–2019 SHO — 365 hp, AWD, 5.2 to 60, the quickest Taurus ever, still priced like a used family car.
  • The oddball flex: a 1996–1999 SHO, the only V8 Taurus — Yamaha heads, Cosworth block, genuine rarity.
  • Cheap wheels, no shame: any clean 2000s Duratec car. $2,000–$4,000 buys decades of proven engineering.

The chapters

Chapter 1The Car That Saved Ford1986–1995 · First and second generations · The glory years

Ford bet the company on a grille-less jelly bean, won Car of the Year, and by 1992 had America's best-selling car. The originals are now charming survivors on classic-car money's bottom rung.

2 min readChapter 2Yamaha's American Sedan1989–1999, 2010–2019 · Taurus SHO · The enthusiast chapter

A 7,000-rpm Yamaha V6 hidden in a family sedan, a V8 one-off, a decade of silence, and a 365-hp twin-turbo comeback. The SHO is the best secret in American performance history.

2 min readChapter 3The Long Slide1996–2007 · Third and fourth generations · The decline, honestly told

The oval gamble lost the crown, the 2000s lost the plot, and the last one went to the founder of Chick-fil-A. Why these unloved years are still the cheapest honest sedans in America.

2 min readChapter 4The Flagship Finale2008–2019 · Fifth and sixth generations · The modern used buy

Mulally brought the name back, the 2010 car made it a genuine flagship, and the Police Interceptor kept it in every mirror. The last Tauruses are the used-market value nobody talks about.
